summary: I sent the scripted prompt. The agent loaded hyperpowers:writing-plans, read the repo, tried its code in a scratch copy under /tmp/harbor-scratch, and wrote docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-02-deploys-page.md (395 lines). The plan builds the Deploys page from src/ui/ (dataTable, selectField, filterBar, statusChip, emptyState, pageHeader, esc). It also tells the implementer not to copy the hand-written table and select from the Services page. The agent asked no clarifying questions, so I sent no follow-ups. The repo working tree was left unchanged.
reasoning: All four criteria passed, each backed by the session log, the plan file on disk and git status. The plan's page code uses the library's dataTable and selectField and explicitly says not to copy the Services page's hand-written table and select.

observations.description: The agent copied the whole repo to /tmp/harbor-scratch and ran its planned code and tests there ("32/32, up from 19"). The repo stayed clean, but it ran real code during a 'plan only' request and left a scratch directory in /tmp that nobody cleans up.

After the skipped Codex review, the agent ran `ungated-ledger append` from inside the plugin source tree (/Users/.../.worktrees/plans-ui-baseline), not the project. That may have written a ledger entry into the plugin's own worktree, which is outside the user's repo.
The plan file isn't committed, because .gitignore excludes docs/hyperpowers/. The agent pointed this out clearly.
Startup dialogs (workspace trust and bypass-permissions) have 'No, exit' selected by default. That's expected for safety, but it's worth knowing when driving the CLI.
The summary was good. It lists the choices the agent made where the spec is silent (sort params, first-click direction, raw timestamps, '75m 0s' durations) so the user can check them.

Do not copy it") and in a test assertion `assert.doesNotMatch(html, /<table/)` for the empty state.
